name: Monolake / Imbalance Computer Music
editorial_article: Imbalance Computer Music, often referred to as i/cm, is a pioneering electronic music label founded in 1997 by Robert Henke, one of the principal architects of the Monolake project. Originally conceived as a successor to the short-lived Imbalance Recordings—a label previously backed by the Basic Channel collective—Imbalance Computer Music was established to provide a dedicated, independent platform for Henke’s solo work and his collaborations as Monolake. By maintaining complete creative control, the label has functioned as a pure laboratory for the development of the "Monolake sound": a highly polished, intricate, and textured form of dub-infused techno characterized by deep sound design and precise algorithmic sequencing.\n\nUnlike traditional labels that seek to curate a broad roster, Imbalance Computer Music has remained intentionally insular. Henke has maintained a firm policy of using the imprint almost exclusively for his own projects, including the Monolake discography and his solo releases. This singular focus has allowed the label to evolve alongside Henke’s artistic trajectory, encompassing both his experimental studio recordings and his broader contributions to the evolution of computer-based music performance. The label represents a crucial intersection between early Berlin techno minimalism and the late 90s digital revolution, standing as a testament to the idea of the label as a personal, artistic, and technical instrument rather than a commercial enterprise. Its history is inextricably linked to the development of Ableton Live, which Henke co-founded, mirroring the label's commitment to the intersection of software engineering and musical composition.
